absent: Enabled direct access implementation including device lifetime, block mapping, cache policy and writeback ordering.
Full signature and return contract of walk_hmem_fn beyond device and target node.
Full signature of decompress_fn beyond input buffer and length, and error code meanings.
Actual device logging backend behavior, formatting, concurrency and ordering when enabled.
Device identifier matching semantics, table termination and driver binding rules.
Locking and lifetime rules for direct access layout breaks, folio locks and mapping entry locks.
Timing, preemption and interruptibility guarantees of millisecond, microsecond and ranged sleep helpers.

findings.text: Fallback direct access controls are inert. Query via dax_holder yields absence and creation via alloc_dax reports operation not supported, while release via put_dax and destroy via kill_dax have no effect. Cache control via dax_write_cache is empty and query via dax_write_cache_enabled reports disabled, while dax_synchronous reports enabled. Setters set_dax_nocache and set_dax_nomc and set_dax_synchronous are empty, and recovery write via dax_recovery_write reports zero bytes.

Mapping support via daxdev_mapping_supported has two build variants gated by a sync descriptor flag. One variant accepts at once when the flag is clear, otherwise requires direct access capability of the inode and then follows the device synchronous property. The other variant accepts exactly when the flag is clear and rejects otherwise.

Host and filesystem attachment fallbacks do nothing useful. Host attach via dax_add_host reports success without action and detach via dax_remove_host is empty, while lookup via fs_dax_get_by_bdev yields absence. Acquire via fs_dax_get reports operation not supported and release via fs_put_dax is empty. Busy page queries via dax_layout_busy_page and dax_layout_busy_page_range yield absence, and writeback via dax_writeback_mapping_range reports operation not supported. Entry lock via dax_lock_mapping_entry yields a neutral cookie with empty unlock via dax_unlock_mapping_entry, and folio unlock via dax_unlock_folio is empty.

Direct access folio and mapping tests use host capability. Lock via dax_lock_folio returns an all bits set cookie for direct access hosts and a clear cookie otherwise. Idle test via dax_page_is_idle requires a present page with zero references. Mapping test via dax_mapping requires a present host that passes direct access capability.

Direct access read sections and layout breaks are no operation successes. Entry via dax_read_lock reports success and exit via dax_read_unlock ignores its token. Interval break via dax_break_layout always reports success with empty finalizer via dax_break_layout_final. Whole inode break via dax_break_layout_inode delegates to the interval form over the full signed range with the caller callback.

Memory error translation via dax_mem2blk_err maps hardware poison to input output failure and passes other codes unchanged. Registration via hmem_register_resource is empty. Walk callback type walk_hmem_fn returns status and begins with device and target node parameters, with remaining parameters not shown in the routed line.

Debug lock disable via __debug_locks_off atomically clears the global flag and returns its prior state. Warning helper DEBUG_LOCKS_WARN_ON evaluates its predicate once outside oops context and when true and locks are off and not silenced emits a warning inside instrumentation guards, returning whether the predicate held. Multiprocessor wrapper SMP_DEBUG_LOCKS_WARN_ON equals the base helper in one build and is an empty loop in the other.

Lock diagnostics are disabled in this configuration. Guard __LINUX_DEBUG_LOCKING_H is defined, self test via locking_selftest is an empty loop, display via debug_show_all_locks and debug_show_held_locks is empty, and checks via debug_check_no_locks_freed and debug_check_no_locks_held are empty.

Each decompression header defines its own include guard as true. This holds for guards DECOMPRESS_BUNZIP2_H and DECOMPRESS_GENERIC_H and LINUX_DECOMPRESS_INFLATE_H and DECOMPR_MM_H and DECOMPRESS_UNLZ4_H and DECOMPRESS_UNLZMA_H and DECOMPRESS_UNLZO_H and DECOMPRESS_UNXZ_H and LINUX_DECOMPRESS_UNZSTD_H.
Generic decompression entry decompress_fn is a function pointer returning status and beginning with input buffer and length parameters. Remaining parameters are not shown in the routed line.

Early allocation around malloc_ptr and malloc_count uses static storage markers STATIC_RW_DATA and MALLOC_VISIBLE. Allocation via malloc rejects negative sizes and lazily seeds its pointer from the free area start and aligns upward to eight and carves the requested size, failing with absence when an end limit exists and would be exceeded, otherwise counting the allocation. Release via free decrements the count and when the last allocation is released resets the pointer to the start. Large forms large_malloc and large_free share the same behavior, and marker INIT is empty in this mode.

Kernel mode allocation names map to kernel heap and virtual allocators. Forms malloc and free map to heap allocation with kernel flags, while large_malloc and large_free map to virtual allocation. Marker INIT denotes early init context and marker STATIC is empty.

Busy delay ceiling MAX_UDELAY_MS is five milliseconds. Slack shift max_slack_shift is two. Upper bound USLEEP_RANGE_UPPER_BOUND is derived by shifting the tick duration left by that shift and converting to microseconds.

Delay selection adapts to size and constness. Helper mdelay uses tight busy waiting for small constant counts and otherwise iterates one millisecond busy waits. Helper ndelay rounds nanoseconds up to microseconds and delegates to microsecond busy wait. Helper fsleep uses busy wait up to ten microseconds and ranged interruptible sleep with proportional slack below the upper bound and millisecond sleep above it.

Ranged sleep helpers delegate to a state parameterized core. Helper usleep_range uses uninterruptible state and helper usleep_range_idle uses idle state, while helper ssleep scales seconds to milliseconds and delegates to millisecond sleep. Guard _LINUX_DELAY_H is defined.

Deferred call record delayed_call holds a function pointer taking an opaque argument plus the argument itself. Definition helper DEFINE_DELAYED_CALL creates such a record with both members cleared. Guard _DELAYED_CALL_H is defined.

Deferred call operations manage presence. Setter set_delayed_call stores both function and argument, runner do_delayed_call invokes the function with its argument only when a function is present, and clearer clear_delayed_call removes the function.
Device logging info limits are sixteen characters for subsystem via PRINTK_INFO_SUBSYSTEM_LEN and forty eight for device via PRINTK_INFO_DEVICE_LEN.
Device logging info record dev_printk_info contains fixed size character arrays sized by the subsystem and device limits. Format helper dev_fmt is identity, and guard _DEVICE_PRINTK_H_ is defined.

Device emit helpers are inert in this configuration. Emit via dev_vprintk_emit and dev_printk_emit returns zero, internal printer via __dev_printk and _dev_printk is empty, and per severity printers _dev_emerg and _dev_crit and _dev_alert and _dev_err and _dev_warn and _dev_notice and _dev_info are empty.

Device message indexing and dispatch separates accounting from printing. Helper dev_printk_index_emit records level and format, wrapper dev_printk_index_wrap emits the index then calls the chosen severity printer, generic printer dev_printk emits the index then calls the internal printer, and disabled form dev_no_printk keeps arguments checked in dead code without running.

Per severity wrappers dev_emerg and dev_crit and dev_alert and dev_err and dev_warn and dev_notice and dev_info forward device plus formatted message and extra arguments through the wrapping helper with matching kernel level and format helper.
Debug helper dev_dbg has three build variants. One dispatches through dynamic debug, one prints directly at debug level via the generic printer, and one is fully disabled.

Single shot and ratelimited device logging uses per site state. Helper dev_level_once runs its severity printer at most once via a persistent flag in one build and never runs in the other while still checking arguments. Once family dev_emerg_once and dev_alert_once and dev_crit_once and dev_err_once and dev_warn_once and dev_notice_once and dev_info_once and dev_dbg_once builds on that helper. Ratelimited family dev_level_ratelimited plus dev_emerg_ratelimited and dev_alert_ratelimited and dev_crit_ratelimited and dev_err_ratelimited and dev_warn_ratelimited and dev_notice_ratelimited and dev_info_ratelimited gates printing behind a per site limiter with default interval and burst. Debug ratelimited dev_dbg_ratelimited has dynamic plus limiter and plain plus limiter and disabled variants, and verbose helper dev_vdbg is either an alias of debug or disabled.

Device warning and probe error helpers adapt generic facilities. Helper dev_WARN forwards driver string plus device name and message to the generic warning facility. Helper dev_err_ptr_probe wraps a probe error code and message into an error pointer, and helper dev_err_cast_probe derives the code from an existing error pointer before wrapping.

Table entries for firmware and bus matching carry small fixed layouts. Entry acpi_device_id carries an identifier byte array sized by its length limit together with driver private data plus class and mask words, with helper ACPI_DEVICE_CLASS initializing class and mask. Entry amba_id carries identifier plus mask plus opaque data. Entry ap_device_id carries match flags plus device type. Guards LINUX_DEVICE_ID_ACPI_H and LINUX_DEVICE_ID_AMBA_H and LINUX_DEVICE_ID_AP_H are defined, and alias kernel_ulong_t is defined.
Identifier and match constants are fixed. Length ACPI_ID_LEN is sixteen, while match bits AP_DEVICE_ID_MATCH_CARD_TYPE is one and AP_DEVICE_ID_MATCH_QUEUE_TYPE is two.

Service and auxiliary entries carry names plus driver data. Entry apr_device_id carries a name array sized by its limit plus domain and service identifiers with version and driver private data, with module prefix APR_MODULE_PREFIX. Entry auxiliary_device_id carries a name array sized by its limit plus driver private data, with module prefix AUXILIARY_MODULE_PREFIX. Guards LINUX_DEVICE_ID_APR_H and LINUX_DEVICE_ID_AUXILIARY_H are defined with alias kernel_ulong_t.
Name capacities and module prefixes are fixed. Size APR_NAME_SIZE is thirty two with an apr tag plus colon prefix, and size AUXILIARY_NAME_SIZE is forty with an auxiliary tag plus colon prefix.

Interconnect and channel entries carry fixed identifier words. Entry bcma_device_id is packed and two byte aligned and carries manufacturer plus identifier plus revision plus class, with macro BCMA_CORE initializing all four members. Entry ccw_device_id carries match flags plus control unit type and device type plus control unit model and device model plus driver info. Guards LINUX_DEVICE_ID_BCMA_H and LINUX_DEVICE_ID_CCW_H are defined with alias kernel_ulong_t for the channel header.

Wildcard and match constants are fixed. Manufacturer and identifier wildcards BCMA_ANY_MANUF and BCMA_ANY_ID are sixty five thousand five hundred thirty five each, while revision and class wildcards BCMA_ANY_REV and BCMA_ANY_CLASS are two hundred fifty five each. Channel match bits CCW_DEVICE_ID_MATCH_CU_TYPE and CCW_DEVICE_ID_MATCH_CU_MODEL and CCW_DEVICE_ID_MATCH_DEVICE_TYPE and CCW_DEVICE_ID_MATCH_DEVICE_MODEL are respectively one and two and four and eight.

Compute and firmware entries carry compact identifier words. Entry cdx_device_id carries vendor and device plus subvendor and subdevice plus class with mask and override only flag. Entry coreboot_device_id carries tag plus driver private data. Entry css_device_id carries match flags plus subchannel type plus driver private data. Guards LINUX_DEVICE_ID_CDX_H and LINUX_DEVICE_ID_COREBOOT_H and LINUX_DEVICE_ID_CSS_H and LINUX_DEVICE_ID_DFL_H are defined, with alias kernel_ulong_t defined for coreboot plus channel subsystem plus DFL headers.
Compute wildcard and override constants are fixed. Wildcard CDX_ANY_ID is sixty five thousand five hundred thirty five, and flag CDX_ID_F_VFIO_DRIVER_OVERRIDE is one.

Silent fallback success and resource limits can mislead callers. Attach via dax_add_host and layout break via dax_break_layout report success while doing nothing, and emit via dev_printk_emit discards messages while returning zero. Early allocation via malloc has no individual release and fails once its arena reaches its end limit, with pointer reset only after a full drain.
